fields.meta_description: Build field service automation that dispatches calls, closes work orders on a phone, moves arrival windows, and books plan visits.
fields.h1: Build Field Service Automation for Your Office and Crews
fields.hero_description: Build field service automation that sends each call to the right technician and closes work orders from a phone.
fields.features_heading: What Field Service Automation Runs for You
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the workflows together with the job records behind them. Diagnosis and repairs stay with your technicians.
fields.feature_1:
Calls matched by zone and certification

Each request from your booking form carries a zip code and a job type. The app offers it to the closest technician certified for that work, then the next one, until someone accepts.
fields.feature_2:
Work orders closed at the customer's door

A technician logs parts and labor against the job on a phone, then hands it over for the customer's signature. The closed work order stays with its job and its customer record.
fields.feature_3:
Customer emails that follow the schedule

The app emails a customer when the technician heads out, and again if the arrival window moves. Each email names the technician and the window, and every send is logged on the job.
fields.feature_4:
Maintenance visits that book themselves

Store each plan's visit dates, and the app opens the work order ahead of each one for the technician who serviced that home last. You pick how many days ahead the work order appears.
fields.feature_5:
Parts and labor synced to QuickBooks

The app connects to QuickBooks, Xero or any tool with an API and sends each closed job's parts and labor lines across for billing. Every job's history sits in a database you own.
fields.feature_6:
The whole app's code in your GitHub

Export the full code of your field service app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can add a parts catalog or a customer portal and keep the work in your own repo.

fields.hero_prompt: Build field service automation for my HVAC company that dispatches calls, closes work orders on a phone, and books plan visits.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up field service automation?

plan.angle: The top 10 are field service software vendors (Oracle, ServicePower, Skedulo, Salesforce, allGeo) and list posts that define the term and list features without showing a single rule an operator could switch on. This page follows one HVAC contractor through four jobs the office does by hand, each with its trigger, its numbers and who hears about it: a no-heat call offered to the nearest furnace-certified technician with 15 minutes to accept, a work order closed on the phone with parts, labor and a signature that syncs to QuickBooks, a job 30 minutes over its booked time that moves the next customer's arrival window, and plan visits due within 21 days turned into work orders.
tab_stories: A no-heat call booked on Dunnachie Heating and Air's website at 7:12 AM is offered to Zbigniew Pazmino, the furnace-certified technician with an open slot in the north zone, and he has 15 minutes to accept before the dispatcher hears about it in Slack.

Ikechukwu Sarkissian closes work order WO-4471 on his phone with two photos, an $86.00 igniter, a $24.00 flame sensor, 1.5 labor hours at $95.00 and the homeowner's signature, and the app syncs the $252.50 total to QuickBooks.

Florimond Gruszka's 1:00 PM repair runs 40 minutes past its booked time, and because any job 30 minutes over moves the next visit, the app emails Rhoswen Cuthbertson a new arrival window of 3:30 PM to 5:30 PM.

Every Monday the app checks 118 maintenance plans, and each plan visit due within 21 days becomes a work order for the technician who serviced that home last; this week 9 qualify and office manager Eulalia Brennagh sees them on one list.
